pending_commit.commit_message: CHROMIUM: arm64: dts: rockchip: Update pwm regulator for rk3399-gru We've adjusted resistors again. Update settings so we get accurate voltages. We go all the way down to the microvolt level now. Though resistors aren't 100% accurate, we might as well take the best numbers we have. BUG=chrome-os-partner:56443 TEST=Build and boot Change-Id: Ifbd0e3a3093a97446c7541d69ba02837936f27cf Signed-off-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/376844 Reviewed-by: Stephen Barber <smbarber@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: arm64: dts: rockchip: Fix period on rk3399-gru pwm-regulators The PWM regulator code was doing all of its math based on a period of 3333 ns. It turns out that after all the math was done and we passed the 3333 ns value to the Rockchip regulator that it decided to use 3337 ns due to rounding. To reduce the math errors, let's just use 3337 ns directly so all our calculations will be slightly more accurate. BUG=chrome-os-partner:56443 TEST=Build and boot Change-Id: I5d5650078f6ce89499bfc76351990f4d372c81f5 Signed-off-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/376846 Reviewed-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: proc: uid_cputime: Store kuid in hash Storing tasks by mapped user IDs doesn't make sense in a system with more than one user namespace. Storing kuids keeps the output consistent, preventing different users running in separate namespaces from being added together. Also this stop leaking all namespace IDs to each reader of the proc file. UPSTREAM: PCI: Don't clear d3cold_allowed for PCIe ports The PCI core skips bridges and ports when the system is suspended. The PCI core checks return value of pci_has_subordinate() in pci_pm_suspend_noirq() to skip all devices where it is non-zero (which means PCI bridges and PCIe ports). Since PCIe ports are never suspended in the first place, there is no need to set d3cold_allowed for them. FROMLIST: i2c: rk3x: Restore clock settings at resume time Depending on a number of factors including: - Which exact Rockchip SoC we're working with - How deep we suspend - Which i2c port we're on We might lose the state of the i2c registers at suspend time. Specifically we've found that on rk3399 the i2c ports that are not in the PMU power domain lose their state with the current suspend depth configured by ARM Tursted Firmware. Note that there are very few actual i2c registers that aren't configured per transfer anyway so all we actually need to re-configure are the clock config registers. We'll just add a call to rk3x_i2c_adapt_div() at resume time and be done with it. NOTE: On rk3399 on ports whose power was lost, I put printouts in at resume time. I saw things like: before: con=0x00010300, div=0x00060006 after: con=0x00010200, div=0x00180025 BUG=chrome-os-partner:56272 TEST=Stylus OK after s2r Signed-off-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> (am from https://patchwork.kernel.org/patch/9304469/) Change-Id: Id3a90892fa5008e1cbbf3edf81c3ad1631a0ae4a Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/377503 Commit-Ready: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> Tested-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Dmitry Torokhov <dtor@chromium.org>

Autotest: Add an Rpc Validator to limit RPCs that can only be called by master. Some RPCs cannot be called by caller except master AFE, or it will lead to db inconsistency between shard and master. This CL fixes this problem by adding an RPC validator to filter such calls from RPC handling side. The validor will refuse any calls whose caller is not master AFE but the target calling method is RPCs in shard.
